paper_metadata.title: Quantum algorithm for credit valuation adjustments

experiments.description: Quantum circuit Born machine (QCBM) training to learn the discretized joint time-price distribution for the CVA state-preparation subroutine on a 4-qubit instance.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) for state preparation
algorithm.ansatz: 2-layer hardware-efficient ansatz with single-qubit Rx/Rz rotations and XX entangling gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Training until cost function convergence; appendix also reports fixed optimization-step counts for different runs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 4 qubits encode the discretized joint state |i,j> over time and asset price; time register m=2 qubits and price register n=2 qubits in the main example
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize clipped negative log-likelihood between model distribution p_theta(x)=|<x|psi(theta)>|^2 and target distribution ptg(x)=P(sj,ti)

problem_instance.description: Single-asset European call CVA instance with geometric Brownian motion price dynamics; target distribution learned from Monte Carlo-binned discretization.

dataset_specification.price_discretization: N=2^n discrete price values; main QCBM example uses n=2

classical_preprocessing: Generate 10^5 Monte Carlo trajectories of asset prices
Bin simulated prices into discrete price values sj
classical_postprocessing: Compare learned distribution to target distribution using KL divergence
Inspect histograms of learned probability distribution

speedup_claims.conditions: for expectation estimation / amplitude estimation in the idealized setting
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes that practical quantum advantage depends on circuit depth, noise, and training quality; QCBM is a state-preparation subroutine rather than the full CVA estimator.

experiments.description: Matrix Product State (MPS) training to learn the discretized joint time-price distribution for the CVA state-preparation subroutine, evaluated across multiple qubit sizes and bond dimensions.

algorithm.variant: Matrix Product State (MPS) generative model for state preparation
algorithm.optimizer: Iterative gradient-based MPS training / DMRG-like scheme
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Stop when KL divergence threshold is reached, objective improvement falls below threshold, or maximum iterations reached

problem_formulation.encoding_details: MPS models the probability distribution over bitstrings x encoding time and price registers; nqubits = n + m
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize L(A) = -(1/|S|) sum_{x in S} log p_A(x), where p_A(x)=|Psi_A(x)|^2

problem_instance.description: Same single-asset European call CVA target distribution as the QCBM experiment; evaluated for nqubits = 4,5,6,7,8,10,12,14,16,20.

classical_preprocessing: Generate target distribution from Monte Carlo simulation
Train MPS on samples drawn from target distribution
classical_postprocessing: Convert trained MPS to quantum circuit via SVD-based isometry construction
Estimate CNOT and single-qubit gate counts

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports training cost scaling empirically as roughly O(n_qubits^6) for MPS training, but does not claim a quantum speedup over a classical baseline for this subroutine.

experiments.description: Controlled Rotation Circuit Ansatz (CRCA) training to approximate the payoff, default probability, and discount-factor controlled rotations used in the CVA circuit, compared against reversible logic synthesis (RLS) resource costs.

algorithm.ansatz: Sequential single-qubit rotation ansatz with Ry, Rz, and Rx gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Training until approximation error is acceptable; exact stopping rule not specified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Discrete index i controls a single-qubit rotation that encodes f(x_i) into ancilla amplitude

problem_instance.description: CVA controlled-rotation subroutines for the same single-asset European call benchmark; resource comparison reported for a 7-qubit total CVA instance and a 4-qubit register example for CRCA gate counts.

classical_preprocessing: Implement function oracle Uf via reversible logic synthesis
classical_postprocessing: Compare CRCA approximation error to exact SU(2) block rotations

speedup_claims.conditions: for the 7-qubit total CVA instance and the 4-qubit register example discussed in the paper
speedup_claims.caveats: The comparison is for gate count only; the CRCA requires classical optimization and the paper notes that optimization becomes harder as qubit count grows.

experiments.description: Noiseless end-to-end quantum CVA circuit simulation using the trained state-preparation and controlled-rotation subcircuits, producing a quantum estimate of CVA and error decomposition.

algorithm.variant: End-to-end CVA circuit with exact simulation of the prepared quantum state

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Time register m=2 qubits, price register n=2 qubits, plus three ancilla qubits for payoff, default probability, and discount factor

problem_instance.description: Same single-asset European call CVA benchmark with discretized price and time; exact quantum-circuit simulation reported.

classical_preprocessing: Exact simulation of the trained quantum circuit
classical_postprocessing: Convert observable expectation to CVA estimate

speedup_claims.conditions: ideal amplitude estimation / expectation estimation setting
speedup_claims.caveats: The actual noiseless end-to-end circuit estimate is 1.987e-05, with dominant error from state preparation and discretization; the paper does not claim demonstrated runtime advantage for this exact simulation.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/epsilon_S) for amplitude estimation; ELF runtime interpolates between O(1/epsilon) and O(1/epsilon^2) depending on noise

experiments.description: Concrete resource estimation for ELF-based Bayesian amplitude estimation applied to the CVA circuit under fault-tolerant assumptions, including logical qubits, logical two-qubit gates, surface-code overhead, and runtime crossover versus classical Monte Carlo.

algorithm.variant: Engineered Likelihood Function (ELF) Bayesian amplitude estimation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Bayesian inference loop until posterior over theta is sufficiently concentrated
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial Gaussian distribution over eta/theta; parameters x_j optimized each round to maximize information gain

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same 7-qubit CVA state-preparation circuit A = eRp eRq eRv eGP, with ELF reflections U(x)=exp(ixPi) and V(y)=A exp(iy|0><0|) A^dagger

problem_instance.description: Same single-asset European call CVA benchmark; runtime estimated for varying target relative errors and hardware code distances.

noise_model.noise_description: fault-tolerant resource model with physical gate error rate 10^-3

classical_preprocessing: Run Monte Carlo with 10, 100, 1000, 10000, or 100000 paths
classical_postprocessing: Compute CVA from discretized time sum
Compare runtime and relative error against quantum runtime model

speedup_claims.conditions: for the example with code distance 18, physical gate error rate 10^-3, surface-code cycle time 1 us, and target relative error 0.001%
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a model-based resource estimate, not an experimental hardware benchmark; the paper also states that for larger relative errors the quantum algorithm is slower, and the crossover depends strongly on hardware assumptions.

speedup_claims.factor: linear in inverse error in low-noise limit; quadratic in high-noise limit
speedup_claims.conditions: ELF Bayesian amplitude estimation under the noise model in Eq. (44)
speedup_claims.caveats: The runtime interpolation depends on the noise parameter λ and assumes fault-tolerant overhead modeled by surface code.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Low-noise limit O(1/epsilon); high-noise limit O(1/epsilon^2)
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Includes surface-code overhead and logical gate time
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: M = 136 logical two-qubit gates per ELF layer; R0(y) uses 8(n+m+2) two-qubit gates and U(x) uses 4 two-qubit gates
complexity_analysis.total_operations_classical: 10^5 Monte Carlo paths for benchmark CVA
